overview: The guide supports reading and search with system fonts and compressed assets. Prioritize the search dialog’s label and response to device theme changes. Build automation has a duplicate trigger path; image sizing and narrow-screen controls need investigation. Findings cover three pages and one search task. The supplied code has not been matched to the live deployment; confirm that match before using it to locate fixes. Passes cover only the stated checks, and unknowns are evidence gaps.
nextSteps: Give the search dialog a unique input ID and matching label, then verify both search forms from the results page.
Test device theme changes with no saved theme choice, correct the live response, and verify that manual choices still take precedence.
Compare push and pull-request runs for one Renovate update before adjusting workflow triggers or cancellation.
At 360 CSS pixels wide, exercise navigation and language options; separately compare one smaller instructional image at 1× and 2× pixel densities.
Ask maintainers for hosting evidence, dependency lock contents, and any performance limits with instructions for responding when they are exceeded.

findings.title: Give the search dialog its own input label
findings.summary: The search-results page contains two inputs with the same search ID. Both Search labels point to the page input, leaving the dialog input without an associated label or explicit accessible name.
findings.whyItMatters: This can make the search field harder to identify with assistive technology when visitors reopen search from the results page.
findings.action: Give the dialog input a unique ID and matching label target. Open the dialog from search results and verify the computed accessible names and operation of both search forms.

findings.title: Follow device theme changes while reading
findings.summary: All three sampled pages open correctly in dark mode when the device already requests it. Changing that preference while a page is open leaves the light colors in place; reading content remains available.
findings.whyItMatters: Visitors changing their device theme do not receive the corresponding reading appearance on the open page.
findings.action: Repeat the change with no saved theme override, then correct the theme-change handling. Verify that pages still open correctly in dark mode and retain an explicit manual theme choice.

findings.title: Avoid duplicate checks for Renovate updates
findings.summary: The supplied build workflow responds to both Renovate branch pushes and pull requests, creating a path for the same checks to run twice. It has no event guard or concurrency cancellation; actual overlap has not been checked.
findings.whyItMatters: Overlapping runs could repeat build and test work without adding distinct validation. Their frequency and resource use have not been measured.
findings.action: Compare paired runs for one Renovate pull request. If they duplicate validation, add an appropriate event guard or cancellation policy while retaining the required build and test checks.

findings.title: Check whether smaller screenshots remain readable
findings.summary: The four instructional screenshots on Manage images use 900-pixel-wide sources and display at 320 CSS pixels on narrow screens. Responses already deliver WebP; smaller versions have not been checked for equivalent detail.
findings.whyItMatters: Smaller versions may reduce transferred data, but the interface details must remain useful for following the instructions. Dimensions alone do not establish waste.
findings.action: Compare one smaller version with the current image at narrow-screen 1× and 2× pixel densities. Add responsive image sizes only if the comparison supports them, retaining WebP delivery and readable details.

findings.title: Check narrow-screen language and navigation controls
findings.summary: At the sampled narrow width, reading content remains available and no horizontal page overflow is reported. However, the English control’s recorded position extends beyond the viewport; neither its menu nor mobile navigation was opened.
findings.whyItMatters: The measurements raise a question about reaching these controls, but do not establish clipping or an interaction failure.
findings.action: At 360 CSS pixels wide, open mobile navigation and language options on the home and Manage images pages. Check visibility, keyboard focus and activation, then correct any confirmed clipping or access problem.

checks.title: Does the conference promotion interrupt finding guidance?
checks.summary: No overlays were recorded, and search opens on request. The homepage includes a conference promotion, but its visual competition with finding image guidance remains unassessed.
checks.nextStep: Inspect the homepage while locating Manage images and check whether the promotion obscures or competes with the task.

checks.title: Are feedback and copy choices presented fairly?
checks.summary: Theme, copy options and Happy/Unhappy feedback controls are present. Their defaults, prominence and alternative paths were not tested enough to assess whether they steer visitors.
checks.nextStep: Open the copy options and exercise both feedback choices, comparing their wording, prominence and resulting steps.

checks.title: Keep image guidance clear for editors
checks.summary: The sampled wording identifies the editor audience, explains CMS and organizes image guidance into concrete tasks. Search descriptions connect to those tasks; understanding by new editors still needs user testing.
checks.nextStep: Ask a new editor to follow the focal-area instructions and note any terminology or steps they cannot explain.

checks.title: Keep navigation and control names consistent
checks.summary: The three desktop pages repeat navigation labels and use consistent names for search and theme controls. This supports consistency in the sample without establishing a documented design system.
checks.nextStep: Compare navigation and control names after opening their menus on narrow screens.

checks.title: Does search respect reduced-motion preferences?
checks.summary: No active animations were recorded in the sampled states. The supplied code includes a dialog fade and staggered search results, whose behavior during activation remains untested.
checks.nextStep: Open search and trigger autocomplete with reduced motion enabled and disabled; compare the transitions and their purpose.

checks.title: Keep reading free of unwanted notification prompts
checks.summary: No notification permission requests or unwanted notification interactions were recorded during reading and search. Browser permission was already denied, so behavior with permission unset remains untested.
checks.nextStep: Observe a longer reading session with notification permission initially unset.

checks.title: Is the printed image guide usable?
checks.summary: Print settings hide primary navigation and retain task headings and all four instructional images. Page breaks, clipping and image readability have not been inspected; no downloads were listed.
checks.nextStep: Inspect Manage images in print preview for awkward page breaks, clipped content and readable image details.

checks.title: Which code remains unused after real tasks?
checks.summary: Some script functions did not run during the short initial observation. Search, mobile navigation and copying need code later, so these results do not identify anything safe to remove.
checks.nextStep: Measure code use through search, mobile navigation, copying and feedback before proposing removal.

checks.title: Could an interactive feature load when needed?
checks.summary: The supplied page template includes search and global scripts, and the recorded search task succeeds. The evidence does not establish which features could load later without affecting their operation.
checks.nextStep: Map scripts to initial and later interactions, then prototype loading one suitable feature on demand and test its activation.

checks.title: Are narrow-screen menus fully reachable?
checks.summary: Narrow layouts retain reading content and shrink images without reported page overflow. The English control extends beyond the recorded viewport, and menu operation remains untested.
checks.nextStep: Open navigation and language options at 360 CSS pixels wide and check clipping, focus and activation.

checks.title: Where would resource-use guidance help editors?
checks.summary: Manage images explains formats, compression defaults and upload limits. The evidence does not identify a consequential choice in this reading task that needs additional environmental information.
checks.nextStep: Identify one real editor decision where supported resource-use advice would change the outcome before adding more guidance.

checks.title: Keep the route from search to image guidance working
checks.summary: Opening search, entering images, pressing Enter and selecting Manage images reached the expected page and instructions. This confirms the recorded task, while its ease and efficiency for editors remain untested.
checks.nextStep: Repeat the task with a representative editor and note hesitation or unnecessary steps.

checks.title: Would smaller instructional images preserve useful detail?
checks.summary: Four 900×666 images display at about 756×559 on desktop and 320×237 on narrow screens, without responsive source alternatives. They arrive as WebP; the readability of smaller versions remains unverified.
checks.nextStep: Compare one smaller version at narrow-screen 1× and 2× pixel densities before changing image delivery.

checks.title: Keep the system-font approach readable
checks.summary: The sampled English pages use a system-font stack and make no initial font downloads, avoiding a web-font loading dependency.
checks.nextStep: Check readability and fallback fonts on another supported operating system.

checks.title: Correct the search dialog’s label association
checks.summary: The search-results page has duplicate search input IDs. Both labels attach to the page field, leaving the dialog field without an associated label or explicit accessible name.
checks.nextStep: Assign the dialog field a unique ID and matching label, then verify both fields’ accessible names with the dialog open.

checks.title: Keep metadata appropriate to each page
checks.summary: Home and Manage images have descriptive titles, descriptions and matching canonical URLs. Search is marked noindex. Structured data parses as JSON, but its validity against the intended schema has not been checked.
checks.nextStep: If structured data serves a required integration, validate one block against its intended schema.

checks.title: Update the theme when the device preference changes
checks.summary: Dark mode works when pages first open with that preference. All three pages retain light colors after a live preference change; their reading content remains present.
checks.nextStep: Test without a saved theme override, correct live changes and verify that manual theme choices still take precedence.

checks.title: Keep core guidance available without JavaScript
checks.summary: Fresh visits without JavaScript retain the sampled reading text, headings, navigation and search results. Operation of the search dialog and other enhancements without scripts was not established.
checks.nextStep: Follow the Manage images navigation link in a fresh session with JavaScript disabled.

checks.title: Are search requests proportionate to typing?
checks.summary: No background API requests were recorded on initial load. The supplied search code waits briefly after typing before requesting results, but interactive request repetition and pending-request handling remain unmeasured.
checks.nextStep: Record requests while typing and revising one search query, including what happens to requests still in progress.

checks.title: Verify that repeat visits reuse public assets
checks.summary: Versioned scripts and styles declare long-lived public caching. Instructional images provide headers for checking whether cached versions are current and distinguishing formats; actual reuse and offline access were not measured.
checks.nextStep: Reload with a warm cache and verify asset reuse and correct image-format selection.

checks.title: Keep compression enabled for text assets
checks.summary: Successful HTML and translation-script responses use Brotli, while the main stylesheet and JavaScript use gzip. The sampled material text assets are compressed.
checks.nextStep: Verify compression when introducing a substantial new text, script or stylesheet asset.

checks.title: Extend keyboard testing through the search dialog
checks.summary: The initial Tab sequence reaches the skip link, home link, search toggle and navigation with a recorded blue focus outline. Dialog operation, reverse navigation and focus traps remain outside this test.
checks.nextStep: Complete search using only the keyboard, then close the dialog and check that focus returns appropriately.

checks.title: Connect the sustainability statement to guide-specific work
checks.summary: Wagtail’s public sustainability statement explicitly includes guide.wagtail.org and describes mitigation approaches. It establishes disclosure; it does not verify implementation or provide this guide’s measured footprint.
checks.nextStep: Review the complete roadmap for dated commitments specific to the guide.

checks.title: Provide a discoverable carbon.txt route
checks.summary: Both tested carbon.txt locations returned 404, with no redirect or delegation found. This fails the sampled discovery check without establishing anything about the site’s emissions.
checks.nextStep: Confirm the intended publication or delegation route with the owner, then publish and validate the carbon.txt information.

checks.title: What evidence covers the guide’s actual hosting?
checks.summary: The supplied material does not establish the live hosting provider, region or energy evidence. Dockerfile comments mention Heroku, but do not verify the operational hosting arrangement.
checks.nextStep: Obtain the service’s deployment identity and provider evidence covering its actual region and reporting period.

checks.title: Maintain shared interface components
checks.summary: The supplied templates share header, theme, footer, navigation and search composition. JavaScript also shares component initialization, supporting reuse in the inspected code.
checks.nextStep: Record the deployed build’s source revision so maintainers can locate these shared components reliably.

checks.title: Can dependency versions be reproduced?
checks.summary: Manifests list dependencies, and build commands request locked installations. Only lock-file names, sizes and hashes were supplied, so valid version resolution and manifest consistency remain unverified.
checks.nextStep: Provide lock-file headers and relevant resolved dependency entries, then check their consistency with the manifests.

checks.title: Keep declared runtime versions aligned
checks.summary: The supplied project, container and development declarations consistently select Python 3.14 and Node 26. This establishes declaration consistency, while deployed versions and latest-stable status remain unverified.
checks.nextStep: Record deployed runtime versions and consult authoritative release references before describing them as the latest stable versions.

checks.title: Remove confirmed overlap between build triggers
checks.summary: Renovate pushes and pull requests can trigger the same build and test jobs, without an event guard or cancellation. The duplicate trigger path is established; actual run overlap and consumption are unmeasured.
checks.nextStep: Inspect paired runs for one Renovate update, then adjust triggers or cancellation while retaining required validation.

checks.title: Keep maintenance instructions usable
checks.summary: The supplied documentation explains setup, development, formatting, linting, testing, translations and version maintenance. It documents the process without establishing how regularly it is followed.
checks.nextStep: Ask a maintainer to check the setup and release instructions against one recent change.

checks.title: Keep release information useful to editors
checks.summary: The supplied Wagtail 8.0 release page identifies its version and modification date and explains editor-facing changes. Live navigation includes versioned releases; publication of this exact text remains unverified.
checks.nextStep: Compare the published Wagtail 8.0 release page with the supplied content.

checks.title: What limits trigger performance action?
checks.summary: The selected build configuration and documentation include linting and build commands, but show no concrete performance limit with a response when exceeded. Limits may exist elsewhere.
checks.nextStep: Request the performance-budget configuration or owner-confirmed policy, including the limit, responsible person and response to an exceedance.

checks.title: Keep reuse terms and contribution routes clear
checks.summary: The supplied license permits code redistribution under stated conditions, and contribution guidance covers code, content and translations. This does not establish licensing for all content or media, or ongoing upstream contributions.
checks.nextStep: Confirm content and media licensing separately before reusing those materials.
